name: IEC ripple counter (RCTRm)
summary: IEC counter marked RCTRm: an asynchronous ripple-carry counter with a cycle length of 2 to the power m.
description: RCTRm identifies an asynchronous or ripple-carry counter of m bits. Each stage clocks the next, so outputs change one after another rather than simultaneously. The clock input carries a dynamic mark, and a clear input is usually shown as an asynchronous R.

Ripple counters are used where outputs are not decoded together at high speed, such as long frequency dividers or simple timers. Drawing them with RCTR rather than CTR warns a reviewer that decoding several outputs together may produce brief false states.
The symbol does not state the cumulative delay through the stages. That depends on the logic family and the number of bits.
readingNotes: RCTR warns that outputs settle in sequence.
Avoid decoding multiple outputs without synchronisation.
drawingChecklist: Show the clear input and its polarity.
Note any decoding that relies on stable outputs.
distinction: CTRm counters are synchronous and all outputs change on the same clock edge.
